summary: Law Minister and Attorney-General Tan Sri Abdul Kadir Yusof said (New Straits Times, 22 July 1977) that he would table a bill establishing a 200-mile exclusive economic zone and that Malaysia would negotiate the zone's limits with other South China Sea states, naming Vietnam; in a Business Times interview published on 5 August 1977 he said Malaysia would soon start charting the zone, that he had told Vietnam's delegate at the last Law of the Sea session of Malaysia's intention, and the paper noted that Malaysia's claims off Sabah and Sarawak might include the disputed Spratly Islands.
actors: Minister of Law and Attorney-General Tan Sri Abdul Kadir Yusof
reasoning: A ministerial public announcement of an intended 200-mile EEZ in the South China Sea, notified to Vietnam and potentially overlapping Vietnam's Spratly claim, is a verbal assertion of new maritime jurisdiction: declarative, and the first such statement found for Malaysia. The newspaper articles were not reachable, so the source is the US embassy's reports of them (cables of 25 July and 16 November 1977); the two dates are the two press reports.

summary: After finding that the Malaysian marker laid on Amboyna Cay in 1975 had disappeared and a Vietnamese monument dated 1976 stood there, Malaysian forces re-erected a 'Pulau Kecil Amboyna' sign on the cay on 11 October 1977 to show Malaysia's claim; Directorate of National Mapping personnel then pressed on with surveys and markings at Swallow Reef and other nearby features.

reasoning: Re-marking a feature already marked by Vietnam, followed by survey and marking of other claimed reefs, is unilateral physical administration without confrontation: demonstrative, and wider in scope than 1975. A contemporaneous US embassy cable of 19 October 1977 confirms that a Malaysian survey vessel had found a Vietnamese claim marker on Amboyna and that the Foreign Ministry had begun a high-level review of the Spratly claims (a government meeting followed on 27 October 1977). Dates conflict: Lai et al. give 11 October 1977, while a retired RMN commando quoted by the NST (2019) and Dzurek (1996) place the landing and marker in 1978. actors: Minister of Law Hamzah Abu Samah
reasoning: A ministerial statement asserting coming EEZ jurisdiction and conditioning foreign access is a verbal claim to maritime rights (declarative). It is general rather than aimed at a named South China Sea rival, so it is a marginal, low-confidence candidate; it repeats the 1977 announcement with more emphasis on exclusive rights.

summary: During Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Van Dong's official visit to Malaysia on 12-16 October 1978, Prime Minister Hussein Onn raised with him the presence of Vietnamese troops on Amboyna Cay; Pham Van Dong promised to study the matter and agreed that conflicting claims should be settled peacefully through negotiation.
reasoning: A head-of-government representation objecting to another claimant's troops on a Malaysian-claimed feature is a verbal diplomatic assertion: declarative, and the first recorded Malaysian démarche on the Spratlys. The Hansard answers (Dewan Negara 10 and 14 April 1980, Dewan Rakyat 10 June 1980) give only 'October 1978'; the visit dates 12-16 October come from a US embassy cable, which does not itself mention Amboyna, so the exact day is unknown.

summary: On 21 December 1979 Malaysia published the two-sheet 'Map Showing Territorial Waters and Continental Shelf Boundaries of Malaysia' (Peta Baru), whose Sabah-Sarawak sheet enclosed about a dozen Spratly features, among them Amboyna Cay (held by Vietnam) and Commodore Reef (later held by the Philippines), within Malaysia's territorial waters and continental shelf.
reasoning: An official map formally claiming disputed Spratly features is a legal and administrative claim statement: declarative, and the founding document of Malaysia's Spratly claim. In 1980 Vietnam sent a protest note (Dewan Rakyat, 10 June 1980), Singapore protested on 14 February 1980 over Pedra Branca, and the UK protested for Brunei over Louisa Reef (Dzurek 1996). The first source is the Law Minister's Dewan Rakyat answer of 17 June 1980 giving the publication date; the Lai et al. source is a PDF.
